title: The Educated Barbarian: Hagakure analysis (part. 16)
summary: NH continues Hagakure with passages on pointless talk in crises, gossip, calm versus agitated men, seeing the world as a dream, poisonous wisdom, compassion, the Dunning-Kruger effect and the feminization of young samurai. He extends the last one into his views on modern masculinity and violence.
claims: Talking endlessly about a problem soothes you into inaction; act instead, and do not talk about what you cannot influence
Constant pandemic talk only spreads and feeds fear
Gossip, positive or negative, wastes time better spent on your own training and capabilities
Agitation and attention-seeking signal insecurity; calmly occupying a space signals self-confidence
Living as in a dream, without fear of death or others' opinions, enables confident, dominant action
True nihilism removes the gravity of life to give back meaning to being human; it has been co-opted into whiny meaninglessness
Intelligent liars are far more dangerous than stupid ones because they can project consequences and keep lies consistent
Intellectual dishonesty and circular arguments mean someone uses intellect never to be wrong; talking to them is a waste of time
He would take someone stupid but sincere over someone intelligent but insincere
Losing quickly can be more honorable than a long, costly defeat
Alphas gain position through force but keep it through compassion; anyone claiming to be an alpha is not one
Strong, secure people tend to be kind; meanness comes from self-hatred, so extend compassion to those who are mean
The Dunning-Kruger effect: those who know least are most confident; the most knowledgeable are the most modest
If you are good at something you do not need to tell people; they will tell you
He believes biology drives sex differences and that society as a whole is becoming more feminized, not men and women crossing
Violence is neutral; men's greater propensity for it can protect, and masculinity can be good or evil
If good men are pacified, no one remains to stop bad men
Suppressing physical violence does not remove it; it morphs into mental and psychological violence
Without assertiveness and aggression you will not train hard or grow as a warrior
Men tend to be risk takers and women stabilizers; men who only protect what they have stagnate
